thread:
dev_lead: kicking off scheduled deploy for llm-router v6 at 02:00 UTC. plan: enable llm_route_v6=5% on canary-global, soak 20m then gradual ramp to 40% if no signals.
deploy-bot: Deploy job started: deploy/llm-router/v6 -> canary-global. CI green, smoke tests passed. auto-ramp plan loaded. link: https://ci.redwood/job/llm-router/9001
pm_jess: noted. putting sticky_session=true for canary and tagging release notes: 'kvcache-bounds, threadpool-adjust'.
qa_lee: FYI ran stress with long seqs; saw slight mem drift but within tolerance on my local harness. will stand by for canary telemetry.
oncall_sam: I'll watch infra and set aggressive auto-hold: p95 mem +4% or error rate >0.2% -> pause.
deploy-bot: 02:05 UTC: ramp to 5% complete. telemetry: errors 0.01%, latency flat, mem +1.2%.
dev_lead: seeing a small number of GC tail events on a subset of canary nodes. not critical yet.
infra_mai: pinned canary nodes to v6 and enabled extra heap metrics.
oncall_sam: 02:12 UTC: canary-node-4 p95 mem +3.8% but stable. holding for additional 10m of soak per plan.
qa_lee: collecting traces for the GC tails and larger seq requests. nothing glaring in stack traces so far.
dev_lead: please keep ramp paused if any host crosses +4.5% for more than 2m.
oncall_sam: 02:20 UTC: canary-node-7 now at p95 mem +4.6% and GC pause 180ms. initiating manual HOLD.
deploy-bot: Hold acknowledged. ramp paused at 5%. snapshot saved. rollback command available: /deploy rollback llm-router --to-version v5 --scope canary-global
pm_jess: propose 10m soak while dev triages. if any host >= +5% for 2m -> rollback. notify maintenance list.
dev_lead: agree. I'm pulling heapdumps from node-7 and node-4. will try to reproduce locally.
qa_lee: running targeted perf with seq_len=4096 to stress kv-cache. will report in 7m.
oncall_sam: 02:27 UTC: node-4 trending to +5.1% and sustained. please be ready to rollback; executing pre-rollback checklist now.
infra_mai: captured core + thread dump. pausing any automated scaling to avoid masking the issue.
deploy-bot: pre-rollback checks complete. rollback ready: /deploy rollback llm-router --to-version v5 --scope canary-global --force
dev_lead: given the metrics, execute rollback. prefer safety here.
pm_jess: executing rollback. also setting flag llm_route_v6=0 for canary cohort to prevent re-traffic. /flag set llm_route_v6 0 --cohort=canary-global --reason="canary mem regression"
deploy-bot: Executing rollback: /deploy rollback llm-router --to-version v5 --scope canary-global --force
oncall_sam: 02:31 UTC: rollback started. draining canary nodes. will monitor for errors.
infr_mai: traffic shifted, memory returning to baseline on affected hosts.
qa_lee: no user-facing errors observed during rollback. test harness shows clean recovery.
pm_jess: release notes updated: "v6 canary rollback due to small memory regression in kv-cache under long sequences; investigation in progress."
dev_lead: next steps: (1) dev to root-cause kv-cache growth, (2) add regression test with seq_len >= 4096, (3) plan a muted reattempt with additional observability and tighter auto-hold.
oncall_sam: opening incident ticket with attached metrics and heapdumps. lowering canary auto-hold threshold for next try.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete at 02:34 UTC. Canary traffic restored to v5. thread kept for postmortem and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
